title: Projects & Kanban
description: Kanban-style projects, tasks, auto-run with the agent, business linking, and the Databases sub-view.

steps.title: Create your first project
steps.body:
Open the **Projects** tab and click **+ New Project**. Give it a name. The kanban opens with three default columns: To Do, In Progress, Done.

Projects are the unit of organized work. Anything the agent does that takes more than one prompt — a refactor, a research run, a multi-step deliverable — should live in one.

steps.title: Add tasks the agent can run
steps.body:
Click `+` on a column to add a task. A task is just a card with a title, description, and (optionally) a checklist.

The magic: drag a task to **In Progress** and click the ⚡ **Run** button. The agent reads the task, plans, and executes — running shell commands, editing files, searching the web — until the checklist is satisfied. You watch the live log; you can pause/cancel any time.

If the agent hits a destructive action (delete, force-push), it stops and asks your approval via Telegram (when configured).

steps.title: Criticality + GitHub precheck
steps.body:
When you click Run, the agent classifies the task by criticality (low / medium / high / critical). Higher criticality triggers an approval gate before any code lands.

If the project is linked to a GitHub repo, a precheck runs first: pulls latest, ensures clean working tree, confirms the branch matches the project's expected branch. Failures block the run instead of merging into a dirty state.

steps.title: Link a project to a business
steps.body:
Open the project's **Edit** dialog. The **Linked business** dropdown scopes the project to one of your businesses (Settings → Business). Once linked:

- The project shows in the business's command center
- The agent treats the business's context as primary when running tasks
- Income tracking ties to that business

Unlinking is reversible — click `(none)` to clear.

steps.title: Databases — the Notion-style sub-view
steps.body:
Inside Projects there's a **Databases** sub-view (top tabs). These are flexible tables: rows + custom properties (text, select, relation, etc.). Use cases:

- A clients database with `name, status, mrr, owner`
- A research database where each row is a paper + tags
- An inventory tracker, content calendar, anything tabular

The agent can query and write to databases via tool calls — *"Add a row to my clients DB for Acme Corp"* just works. Each database can also sync two-way with Notion if you've connected it.

steps.title: Reviewing what the agent did
steps.body:
Every run leaves a trail:

- **Activity tab** — every tool call the agent made, in order
- **Files tab** (in the project) — every file the agent created/changed, diffable
- **Checkpoints** — the agent snapshots state before risky operations; you can roll back to any checkpoint

If something went sideways, restoring a checkpoint is a single click.
